Frequently Asked Questions

Does it really work for mice?

The PestLab Pest Repeller emits ultrasonic and electromagnetic signals designed to make the environment uncomfortable for rodents, including mice and rats. Many customers report noticing fewer signs of activity within the first few days. Individual results depend on the size of the room, the severity of the problem, and correct placement.

How many devices do I need?

PestLab recommends one device per room. The ultrasonic signals do not pass through walls, so each room where you have seen signs of mice should have its own unit. Most customers start with 3 to 6 devices.

Is it safe around my pets?

Yes. The device uses no chemicals, no poison, and no bait. It is designed to be safe for dogs, cats, and other household pets when used as directed. The ultrasonic frequencies are outside the hearing range of cats and dogs.

How long does it take to work?

Many customers report noticing a difference within 2 to 7 days. The speed depends on the severity of the problem. For heavy infestations, PestLab recommends giving it up to 2 to 3 weeks.

Will it work in my garage or basement?

Yes, as long as there is a standard wall outlet. The device is designed for indoor use and works in kitchens, bedrooms, basements, garages, attics, and storage rooms.

How long does the device last?

The PestLab Pest Repeller is built to last 4 to 5 years of continuous use. There are no batteries to replace, no cartridges to refill, and no moving parts.

What if it does not work for me?

Every order is backed by a 90-day money-back guarantee. If you are not satisfied, contact PestLab support for a full refund, no questions asked.

Does it use a lot of electricity?

No. The device consumes less power than an LED night light. You will not notice any difference on your electricity bill.

Can I move it between rooms?

Yes. The device is portable and works in any standard wall outlet. However, for the best results, PestLab recommends keeping one plugged in per room rather than moving a single device around.

Do I still need to seal holes and gaps?

Sealing entry points is always a good practice. The PestLab device is designed to discourage mice from staying in treated areas, but reducing access points will help improve results.
